title: Facebook, October 4, 2021: One maintenance command takes everything down

subtitle.simple: How a single command made Facebook vanish from the internet for six hours.
subtitle.tech: Backbone outage, audit bug, DNS servers withdraw their BGP routes.

headline.simple: Problem: For six hours, nobody in the world could find Facebook. Why?
headline.tech: Bug: backbone down → DNS withdraws BGP routes → facebook.com does not resolve.

text.simple: You open Facebook. The internet asks Facebook's signpost where the site can be found.
text.tech: The app resolves facebook.com; the query lands at Facebook's DNS servers.

text.simple: The signpost gives the way, and Facebook loads for you.
text.tech: DNS answer with IP address; the route to it is known via BGP.

text.simple: Meanwhile, the signpost keeps checking that it can reach the data centers over the main line.
text.tech: The DNS servers continuously check their connection to the data centers over the backbone.

text.simple: During routine maintenance, a technician gives a command that accidentally turns off all lines.
text.tech: A command meant to measure capacity unintentionally disconnects all backbone links.

text.simple: The checker should stop this, but it has a bug of its own and lets the command through.
text.tech: A bug in the audit tool prevents the command from being blocked.

text.simple: The signpost can no longer reach any data center, so it thinks it is broken itself.
text.tech: The health check fails; the DNS servers mark themselves as unhealthy.

text.simple: So it deletes its route from the internet, even though it is still running.
text.tech: The DNS servers withdraw their BGP routes even though they are still running.

text.simple: You open Facebook again, but the internet no longer knows the way: the site has vanished.
text.tech: facebook.com can no longer be resolved anywhere in the world.

headline.simple: Solution: The repaired checker stops the dangerous command before it reaches the lines.
headline.tech: Fix: audit tool corrected – commands that disconnect the backbone are blocked.

intro.simple: Meta's report gives no details on the repair. Shown here is the obvious one: fixing the checker.
intro.tech: The postmortem names no concrete fix. Shown: a corrected audit tool.

text.simple: The repaired checker spots the danger and sends the command back.
text.tech: The corrected audit tool detects the risk and blocks the command.

text.simple: The main line stays on, and the signpost can still reach the data centers.
text.tech: Backbone stays up; the DNS servers' health check stays green.

text.simple: You open Facebook, and the signpost tells the internet the way as usual.
text.tech: DNS resolution works; the BGP routes stay in place.

text.simple: Result: Facebook stays reachable, and the maintenance does no harm.
text.tech: Result: no outage, no withdrawn routes.
